title: Singing Mama Loves Papa and how he plays rock and roll
summary: Punch sings Mama Loves Papa, says he seldom sings the old numbers and describes how a trumpet fits rock and roll.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Everything is damn as sweet as can be. Nothing to worry, nothing to worry for me, for me. There's a good reason, a quite good reason. Mama Love Squeezing and Paw, us too. Nothing can break us, nothing can make us blue. We have the bungalow and how we spoon in the evening under the silver moon. People like us, we never fuss. We always have something better to do, cause Mama Love Paw and Paw, Paw and Paw and Paw love my Mama too. Okay. Yeah.
Mama Love Paw, Paw, Paw love Mama.
Yeah, sometimes I do. But I don't sing them, no, very seldom. I sing the lady. You sing late now?
Yeah, he knows all the late numbers. You're going to take up rock and roll next, Mark?

No, I know rock and roll, but I can play rock and roll. See, a trumpet ain't got nothing to do but rock and roll with whole notes. The guitar and the drum and bass, violin. They make all this stuff. You just ta, ta, ta, ta, that's all you got to do on drum.
You play lead rhythm on drum. Sure, that's good.
